cards.text: Saul has just been confirmed as king at Gilgal, and everybody's celebrating. Then Samuel, the prophet who's been leading Israel, stands up in front of all Israel. He tells them he listened to everything they said, and he set a king over them.

cards.question: Samuel points to the new king walking before them. Then he talks about himself. How does Samuel describe himself?

cards.text: Then Samuel puts his whole record on trial, right there before the LORD and His anointed. Friend, if I tried that, the dead batteries I shared that drawer with would STILL be lined up to complain.

cards.question: Samuel asks the people if he ever took anyone's ox or donkey, cheated anyone or took a bribe. If he did, what does he promise to do?
When Samuel asks, the people say he cheated or oppressed some of them.

cards.text: Samuel says the LORD and His anointed are witnesses that nobody found anything in his hand, and the people agree. Friend, that's a cleaner record than my apron has EVER had.
Then Samuel flips it around. Now he's going to confront them before the LORD with all the righteous acts the LORD has done for them and their fathers.

cards.question: Samuel starts back when Jacob went to Egypt and the fathers cried out to the LORD. Whom did the LORD send them?

cards.text: Moses and Aaron brought the fathers out of Egypt and settled them right here in this place. You'd think that's the happy ending, friend. Hold on.

cards.question: Once the fathers are settled in the land, how do they treat the LORD their God?

cards.text: So He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab. Sisera, the Philistines AND Moab is not a rough week, friend, that's a whole rough lineup.

cards.question: Under all that pressure, the fathers cry out to the LORD. What do they confess?

cards.text: They admit they served the Baals and Ashtoreths, and they ask Him to deliver them so they can serve Him. And the LORD answers by sending deliverers.

cards.question: When Samuel lists the deliverers the LORD sent, he names himself too.
The LORD delivered them from their enemies on every side, and they dwelt ___.

cards.text: Then Samuel brings it right up to now. When Nahash, king of the Ammonites, moved against them, they told Samuel no, they had to have a king.

cards.question: Samuel says they demanded a king even though they already had one. Who does Samuel say was already their king?

cards.text: Here's the king they chose, the one they requested, and the LORD has placed him over them. That's the ding on your phone, friend: the thing you ordered is ON the porch.

cards.question: Samuel lays out an if. If the people and their king fear the LORD, serve Him, obey His voice and follow Him, how does Samuel say things will go?
But if they disobey and rebel, Samuel says the hand of the LORD will be ___ them, just like with their fathers.

cards.text: Then Samuel tells them to watch a great thing the LORD will do before their eyes. And he asks them, "Is it not the wheat harvest today?"

cards.question: It's the wheat harvest, and Samuel says he'll call on the LORD to send something. What?
Why does Samuel call for this sign during the wheat harvest?

answers.text: To show the evil of asking for a king
To water the fields for the harvest
To prove the LORD chose Saul

cards.text: Samuel calls to the LORD, and that same day the LORD sends thunder and rain. You finally get a sunny day off, you step outside, and the sky goes BOOM.

cards.question: When the thunder and rain come, all the people greatly ___ the LORD and Samuel.

cards.text: They beg Samuel to pray to the LORD his God for them so they won't die, and they admit they've added the evil of asking for a king to all their sins. When I burn a batch, I don't wait for thunder either, friend. I'm confessing before the smoke alarm finishes.

cards.question: Samuel answers the scared crowd. What does he tell them first?
Samuel tells the people that after all this evil, they should stop following the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, he says, serve the LORD with all your heart, and don't turn aside after worthless things that can't profit you or deliver you, because they're empty. Empty, friend, like a cookie box that looks GREAT until you open the lid.

cards.question: Samuel promises the LORD will not abandon His people, for the sake of His great name. What other reason does he give?

answers.text: He was pleased to make them His own
They promised to serve Him from now on
They finally have a king to lead them

cards.question: Then Samuel talks about himself. He says it would be a sin against the LORD to stop doing something for the people. What?

cards.text: He'll keep teaching them the good and right way, too. Then comes his "Above all": fear the LORD, serve Him faithfully with all your heart, and consider the great things He has done for them.

cards.question: Samuel ends with a warning. If the people persist in doing evil, what happens to them and their king?

answers.text: They will be sent to Egypt

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from the previous passage (Saul confirmed as king at Gilgal, everybody celebrating, from 1 Samuel 11:14-15). The card cites only 1 Samuel 12:1, so those facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card may have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "You'd think that's the happy ending, friend. Hold on." tells the baker something bad comes next. That rules out the two positive wrong answers on card 10 ("They build Him a temple" and "They fear Him more") and leaves only "They forget Him."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer "They had forsaken the LORD" is the only one that mentions the LORD, and it uses Bible-sounding wording ("forsaken"). The wrong answers "They had lost their courage" and "They had broken a treaty" are plain and leave God out, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Verse 11 names the deliverers the LORD sent: Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah and Samuel. The card only says "sending deliverers", and no card ever names Jerubbaal, Barak or Jephthah. Card 14 then refers to Samuel's list of deliverers, which the baker never heard.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the stop's 8 choice cards. True or false has 2 and fill in the blank has 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question asks why Samuel calls for the sign during the wheat harvest. Verse 17 gives a reason for the sign itself (so they will know the evil of asking for a king). It never says why the timing is the wheat harvest, so the question claims the text explains something it leaves open.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences, and it carries two beats: the people's plea and confession, plus a separate joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "When I burn a batch, I don't wait for thunder either" says the people didn't wait for thunder. But in 1 Samuel 12:18-19 they confess only after the thunder and rain come. The word "either" makes the joke contradict the moment, so the comparison doesn't share the core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 8 of the stop's 11 choice cards. Fill in the blank has 2 and true or false has 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
